model_statements: Walking time is the Tobler (1993) hiking function integrated over 5 m DEM gradient cells along the time-optimal route on the trusted subgraph: a modelled minimum, not a measured pedestrian time.

Terrain effort is the Minetti et al. (2002) cost of walking integrated the same way along the effort-optimal route (J/kg). Effort, time and distance are separate objectives and are never combined into a score.

Catchability is a constraint, not an objective: one exact trip is chosen, the stops where slack = trip expected arrival - modelled pedestrian arrival is >= 0 are feasible, and only those stops are compared. Boarding time is not optimised: boarding the same trip upstream is not an earlier arrival.

Expected service times are GTFS-Realtime feed information (an absolute time, or scheduled + delay) matched on the exact trip_id; they are not a prediction made here. One snapshot says nothing about the next one.
A stop whose slack is negative is 'not proven catchable under the current model', never 'missed'.
Scheduled-only times come from the static timetable (calendar-checked) and have not been confirmed by realtime.

next_feasible_trip.policy: trips in chronological order of their reference time; the first with >= 1 realtime-confirmed catchable stop, else the first with >= 1 stop feasible on the static timetable only; 'next' is the trip, not an earliest boarding stop
